title: Expired Safety Interlock Deviation with Conflicting Records
scenario_text:
Context from SAP S/4HANA (Plant 2 — Production Orders):
Order: 4001892 | Material: FORGE-7741-A (high-temp turbine shaft) | Work Center: CNC-14 | Status: CONFIRMED | Safety interlocks: ALL ACTIVE per system check 06/12/2026.

Context from MasterControl (Quality — Deviation Log):
DEV-2025-0087 | Type: Temporary Process Deviation | Equipment: CNC-14 thermal interlock | Approved by: R. Kowalski (EHS Manager) | Effective: 2025-03-14 | Expiry: 2025-09-14 | Status: EXPIRED | Justification: 'Interlock trips at 410°F but new alloy requires 435°F soak. Bypass approved pending engineering review of setpoint change.'

**Microsoft Teams — #plant2-maintenance (Jun 24, 2026, 6:47 AM)**
@tony.reeves: Heads up — CNC-14 thermal kicked again last night on the 3rd shift run. Danny just bridged it like usual and kept running. No scrap.
@miguel.santos: Wait, I thought we closed that deviation last September?
@tony.reeves: Did we? The jumper's still in place from when Bobby installed it. Nobody told us to pull it.
@miguel.santos: ...
[No further replies in thread]

**Paper Logbook — CNC-14 Equipment History (scanned PDF, Plant 2 floor):**
Entry dated 2025-03-15: 'Installed thermal bypass jumper per DEV-2025-0087. Signed: B. Hernandez, Maintenance Tech II.'
No subsequent entry for removal.

**SharePoint — /policies/safety/PSM-MOC-procedure (Page version 3, published Jan 2026)**
Section 4.1: 'Any temporary deviation that alters a safety-critical interlock must be formally closed via MOC process within 30 days of expiration. Failure to close constitutes an unauthorized process change subject to OSHA PSM enforcement.'
[Version 2 (2024) stated: 'Temporary deviations auto-close on expiry date. No further action required.']

**SAP PM — Preventive Maintenance Schedule (CNC-14):**
Last interlock validation: 2026-01-08 | Result: PASS | Performed by: Automated PLC check
Note: PLC validates interlock CIRCUIT CONTINUITY, not functional setpoint. A bridged interlock passes continuity check.

**Email — Subject: 'RE: CNC-14 Setpoint Review' (Sep 2, 2025)**
From: j.park@ironforge-mfg.com (Process Engineering)
To: r.kowalski@ironforge-mfg.com
CC: miguel.santos@ironforge-mfg.com
> Engineering recommends permanent setpoint change to 440°F.
> ECN-2025-1104 drafted but needs capital approval ($8K for new sensor rated to 500°F).
> Holding pending Q4 budget review.

[No follow-up emails found. ECN-2025-1104 status in Jira: OPEN, unassigned, last updated Sep 2025.]
question: A PSM auditor asks: What is Ironforge's current compliance status regarding CNC-14's thermal interlock, and what is the correct immediate action?

contributor.name: Miguel Santos
contributor.title: Plant Operations Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Production scheduling, maintenance planning, safety decisions, equipment change-out approvals, PSM compliance

choices: Non-compliant — the bypass is physically still in place constituting an unauthorized process change under the current PSM-MOC procedure; immediate action is to remove the jumper, halt production on CNC-14, and initiate a retroactive MOC
Non-compliant — but the issue is only that ECN-2025-1104 was never completed; once the permanent setpoint change is approved, the bypass becomes authorized retroactively
Indeterminate — the policy version that was active when the deviation expired (v2, 2024) said deviations auto-close, so no MOC was required at the time; the new policy cannot be applied retroactively
Compliant — the deviation expired in September 2025, meaning the bypass auto-closed per policy, and the January 2026 PM validation confirmed the interlock passed
